Survey Slam. The MJ\'s Story Food, friends, and family is the decade-long mantra of MJ’s Tavern. John & Mike’s vision craved a neighborhood bar that created an environment where everyone could enjoy a home-cooked meal and sip on a refreshing beverage, all while being treated fairly. It seems simple enough, but after the Garage closed, there was no place for all to call home. Food MJ’s Tavern is where your tummy is satisfied with love; reminiscent of Grandma’s kitchen. Made from scratch soups, salad dressings, and desserts served in generous portions for a fair price make MJ’s stand out from those traditional evening nightclub establishments. Craving creamy mashed potatoes with homemade dressing? You’ll have to wait until the potatoes are peeled, cooked, and mashed because they are made from scratch. Fresh salads and the famous Mike’s Grilled Chicken will keep you in swimsuit shape, but when you feel like treating yourself, add freshly baked brownies for dessert. Daily specials include traditional items like tacos and wings sprinkled with neighborhood favorites like fresh raw and roasted oysters. MJ’s house recipes start with an idea, refined by the staff, and tested by the guests. Favorites stay on the menu. Wake up hungry, and don’t forget that MJs also serves breakfast daily from 9 AM – 2 PM. Grab a quick breakfast sandwich and coffee if you’re in a rush, or stay for a while to enjoy a Bloody Mary and Eggs Benedict. Friends The saying goes, friends are strangers one hasn’t met yet, which is surely true at MJ’s Tavern. Mike and John accept everyone so much that all the staff and customers do the same. True friends step up when a friend is in need, and MJ’s is no different. A pillar in the community that reaches out past the Tavern’s four walls, MJ’s has been providing venues for fundraising efforts for over a decade. Food drives, breast cancer outreach functions for families in need, and braving the frigid Atlantic Ocean during the Special Olympics are all examples of how MJ’s demonstrates community service in our neighborhood. MJ’s doesn’t stop at fundraising opportunities. The establishment has united groups with common themes. Stop by MJ’s to grab a meal, and you might see a church or community meeting taking place, too. You might see a group of gals playing Mahjong, and if not, there are plenty of other games to keep the good times rolling. Family Families come together in marriage, and MJ’s has accommodated weddings, too. MJ’s family spans from first-time customers to loyal regulars, staff, and owners. It’s the go-to place to bring your family to relax and enjoy all the benefits of a home-cooked meal without the cleanup! John’s military experience taught him tolerance and the need for diversity. His understanding to see people for who they are is easily seen throughout the restaurant. Before the doors even open, John and Mike have their first round of guests. Their in-house staff members are treated with respect and love and given chances to excel and lead, which builds confidence and loyalty. In turn, the staff treats MJ’s Tavern like their own and welcomes each guest with a friendly face and smile. A true anchor to the success of MJ’s is the incredible family of staff. Whether it’s Martha May, Greg, or George in the kitchen serving up amazing culinary treats, Jamie, Shay, Britanie, Dominick, James, or Brenda behind the bar, or JC serving up hot meals to guests, we would never be where we are today without the hard work and support of our MJ’s Family.

Pub Quiz. On May 18, 1981, a year after Mt. St. Helen\'s blew, Seattle\'s first Irish bar opened: Murphy\'s Irish Pub. That\'s right. We\'ve been around for more than thirty years. When Chris Barnes and Dan Cowan originally opened Murphy\'s, it stood where Starbucks stands today, a half a block to the east (a Radio Shack stood on the corner of 45th and Meridian, where Murphy\'s is today). Dan left shortly after (and went on to open The Tractor Tavern in Ballard), while Chris slowly built a Seattle institution. For years, its stage was host to the nationally syndicated Sandy Bradley\'s Potluck, a sort of Prairie Home Companion of Seattle, featuring traditional old-time American music, ragtime and blues to movie cartoon sound tracks and novelty songs. Being the first Irish pub, it managed to log a few firsts along the way: the first bar in Seattle to start a St. Patrick\'s Day tradition, the first bar in Seattle to pour micro brews from the tap (Redhook opened in Fremont in 1982), and first in the hearts of its patrons all the way. On February 12th, 2015, Murphy\'s Pub reopened under new management and ownership. The new crew is Phil and Chelley Bassett, and Eamonn Davey. After the much needed facelift, you\'ll find that Murphy\'s is still pretty much the same: a bar in the Irish tradition, where you can chit chat with friends over a Guinness or Murphy\'s and other great Northwest beers, dine on great tasting food, listen to some live music a few nights a week (Irish music jam session on Mondays), and just relax after a long day.

Authentically British from the “draught” beers to the darts (not machines, but real darts and dartboards), to the homemade pink-and-yellow-checkered, marzipan-wrapped Battenburg cake that accompanies afternoon tea, Robin Hood British Pub has been a Valley home-away-from-home for relocated Brits for nearly 30 years. It has also been a faithful stand-in as a mini-visit to London for local Anglophiles craving homemade chicken curry pie or true fish ‘n chips.

Londoners Michael and Lorraine Williams began Robin Hood 30 years ago when they bought a run-down beer bar in Sherman Oaks and converted it into a casual place for brews and burgers. After a few years, they added British comfort foods to the menu and began making their own tartar sauce (it’s been getting rave reviews ever since) to accompany the house favorite, fish ‘n chips. Michael, a former pub professional in England, brought in classic draft British beers. An appreciative clientele took root and has been evolving ever since; newcomers and regulars, British and American, unite at Robin Hood in their love of good British food, drink, and camaraderie.

Pub Quiz. Whisk(e)y originates from Gaelic for “water of life”. According to author David Broom, the Scots and Irish Gaelic translation of this is uisge beatha. This referred to a proto-whisk(e)y redistilled with spices and herbs and the straight version became known as \'usky\'.\"

Now is it Whiskey or Whisky? In short, the spelling \"whiskey\" is common in the United States and Ireland. The rest of the world, including Japan, Scotland and Canada, uses \"whisky.\"

Bourbon, Rye, Single Malts, Blends - they\'re all whisk(e)y. There is no one right way to drink all whisk(e)ys. Whether you drink it neat or on the rocks, whisk(e)y is one of America\'s most beloved spirits.  Enjoying this beverage is a personal journey that could easily change from week to week, day to day, drink to drink.

You\'ll find that many whisk(e)ys are greatly enhanced by ice, but you\'d be doing yourself a disservice if you don\'t at least try the whiskey neat. Have you tried your Scotch with a few drops of mineral water?  A splash of water can be a great thing as it releases the hydrophobic elements in the glass, allowing you to detect more aromatics on the nose, and by lowering the alcohol content, it can allow you to taste more flavors on your palate.

At Hops & Scotch we have over 450 types of whisk(e)ys ranging from American Bourbon to Japanese Whisk(e)y.  Whether you like your rye neat or your Scotch with a drop of mineral water, or your bourbon with our ice spheres molded at the bar, Hops & Scotch is sure to have something to please your palate!

The first mention of The Peahen is in 1480, and on the construction of London Road in the 18th Century it was merged with the adjoining pub, The Woolpack. Trading as a hotel, The Peahen was a vital stopping point on the way through to London for tourists and business folk. The original wood building burnt down towards the end of the 19th Century and was rebuilt in its current form as The Peahen Hotel.

Join us on a Tuesday Night at 7.30pm for a splendid quiz night!

There’s never a dull Tuesday here as they’re host to a stellar pub quiz at 19.30 every week!

Once a bank, now made brilliant – welcome to the Cambridge Tap!

They love a really good burger – unique, tender and fresh, served in an all butter brioche bun and perfected. Dirty fries, wings, small plates and sharers – this is the perfect menu for any social gathering.

On Mondays at 8pm, find yourself here for a brain tickling pub quiz!

The Ship Inn was “built” in 1835 it is thought by two houses sandwiched together and made into a pub, it has been a pub all its history surviving until present day. The Great Eastern steam ship was built and launched by Isambard Kingdom Brunel next door at Burrells Wharf in 1858 and the man himself may have frequented The Ship during this time for a cold refreshing beer after a hard day’s work!

Come and join us on a Sunday at 19.30 for a pub quiz in a pub full of charm and history.

Brouge is a welcoming and family friendly Bar and Restaurant with cosy atmosphere, serving delicious fresh food prepared daily, friendly service and a wide range of Belgian and craft beers, great real ales as well delicious wines and cocktails.

Come to the popular pub quiz on a Tuesday at 8pm for the chance to win some prizes!

Perched on the edge of Turnham Green, The Crown & Anchor proudly stands out amongst the many watering holes of Chiswick High Road.

Join them on a Thursday evening at 8pm for a stand out pub quiz!
If you are hitting the town centre, then we have the perfect pit-stop location for you to refuel, featuring 20 taps of epic craft beer, and a pub quiz on Tuesday nights at 7pm!

The Kings Arms, a quintessential real ale pub in one of the most historic streets in London. The multi-winning “pub of the year” site is about as traditional as traditional pubs get, but with a Thai twist coming out of its popular kitchen too.

On a Sunday, from 7:30pm, round off the weekend with a night of trivia at the pub quiz!

Overlooking the Thames, in a peaceful neighbourhood not that far from the bustle of Canary Wharf, The Grapes is one of the oldest pubs in London. Charles Dickens was a patron, and even made reference to the pub in his novel ‘Our Mutual Friend’.

On a Monday at 8pm, come here for one of the most popular pub quizzes in London.

Overlooking Barnes Pond, this pub was originally a Georgian ‘coffee house’ but has sold beer since around 1776. At the heart of the riverside ‘village’ of Barnes on the banks of the Thames, The Sun Inn is an iconic London pub. On a Monday evening, start the week with a bang by joining them for a pub quiz at 8pm and test your luck.

Located in the heart of Berkhamsted, The Highwayman is a spacious pub and brasserie serving a seasonal menu of home-cooked dishes with a French twist.

Come on down at 7.30pm on a Wednesday to get over that hump day hump with a pub quiz!

The Railway is one of Blackheath Village’s most established watering holes. Perfect for refreshment after a day’s sight-seeing nearby.

On a Sunday at 8pm, this pub also boasts a jolly quiz night!

The Pembroke is a friendly pub in Primrose Hill offering delicious food, great drinks and unforgettable experiences.

At 8pm on a Thursday evening, come on down for a pub quiz.

A friendly, cosy, community pub with a welcoming atmosphere and a busy, lively quiz with the bubbly and fun Kat hosting every Thursday at 8pm!

We recommend booking your table for this venue.

The Angel on the Bridge is an iconic pub. Dating back to 1728, this grade II listed pub is one of the most photographed and painted pubs in England, because of its architecture and the amazing riverside location on the River Thames.

On a Wednesday at 7pm you can enjoy their weekly pub quiz!

The Draper’s Arms located in Ealing is a lively Popular Pub offering good beer and delicious food while you admire the timber ceilings and stylish checkerboard floor tiles.

Every Thursday at 7pm, treat yourself to a pub quiz with many prizes to give away.

With Hyde Park right on our doorstep, The Champion is perfectly placed for taking in the sights and sounds of leafy yet vibrant Notting Hill.

At 8pm on a Tuesday evening, you could be walking out with lots of exciting prizes at the weekly pub quiz.

The Pilot is a small but perfectly formed pub, serving up an extremely high standard of food and ale in a friendly, relaxed environment. A building of some history, The Pilot now provides the stylish solution for function hire in Chiswick.

On a Sunday at 7.30pm you can enjoy a cosy pub quiz.

The Trinity Arms is your local home from home, hidden on a stunning square in the heart of Brixton, just a stone’s throw from the hustle and bustle of Brixton High Street, but far enough away to be a welcome retreat!

Every Monday at 8pm join the fabulous and bubbly, Kat, for a fun and lively pub quiz with games, lots of prizes and a roll-over Jackpot Bartab up for grabs!

This popular and trendy pub is a must visit for South London quizzers!

We recommend booking a table for this one!

In June 2014, The Bohemia re-opened this magnificent building in the heart of North Finchley as a London Brewing Company brewpub. They also have an onsite bottle shop including a growler filler for those times when you want to take a little drop of The Bohemia home. At 8pm on a Tuesday evening, The Bohemia is host to a prize-filled pub quiz.

Formerly known as the Black House in the 1970’s, it is located on Holloway Road ‘The Heart of Islington’. The building itself was briefly the start of radical black Britain. Also bizarrely John Lennon and Yoko Ono stood on the roof of the pub swapping their cut hair with a pair of bloodied Muhammed Ali shorts, true story!

Join us on a Tuesday evening at 7.30pm for a lively pub quiz.

Close to the vibrant heart of Shoreditch, possibly the only pub ever to be famed for its name-check in a nursery rhyme. The Eagle is mentioned in the age-old ditty, ‘Pop Goes the Weasel’ – “Up and down the City Road, in and out The Eagle; that’s the way the money goes, pop goes the weasel”.

On a Wednesday at 19:30, this venue hosts a bustling pub quiz.

A beer house since 1836, the Red Lion continues to embrace its grain led origins, recently winning Cambridge CAMRA’s pub of the year award. Tucked away on the outskirts of Cambridge and proudly located in the ever-growing town of Histon.

Every Tuesday at 7pm.

The Fentiman Arms is a buzzy local ideally positioned between Oval, Vauxhall and Kennington tube stations, close enough from the Oval Cricket Ground that you can just hear the roar of cricket fans on match days.

With just £1, you can participate in an exciting pub quiz every Tuesday at 20.00.

Situated high up on the hill and overlooking the common in Chalfont, The Jolly Farmer is at the heart of the community. Inside there is a spacious bar and roomy brasserie from which you can enjoy the views. Serving a menu of seasonal favourites with a French twist.

Every Tuesday at 19.30 come and join the fun at our pub quiz!

The Perseverance is a rare free of tie public house, located in lovely Bloomsbury, only minutes away from Holborn and Russell Square stations.

Brighten up your Monday by coming on down to their weekly pub quiz on Mondays at 7pm.

The Lord Napier Star is certainly the focal point of Hackney Wick, and has been for decades. They’re the only pub in Hackney Wick and pretty hard to miss, they’re the one covered in graffiti.

Hosting a weekly quiz night on Tuesdays at 7.30pm.

venue_name: PUB QUIZ – Star by Hackney Downs, Hackney – Every Tuesday
notes:
Less than a stone’s throw from Hackney Downs park and when you step inside you’ll be transported to an eclectic fairground setting where there’s a wall to wall feast for the eyes.

With a pub quiz every Tuesday at 8pm, what more can you want?

‘Blending the hip and the wholesome – a vibrant British pub offering the warmest of welcomes’.

The castle runs a fun-filled pub quiz on Tuesdays at 7pm.

With a beautiful airy bar, spacious brasserie and a gorgeous covered terrace for dining, serving a seasonal menu of home-cooked dishes with a French twist.

Come and join us at 8pm every Monday for a quiz night in Upminster!

It is thought that there has been a tavern on the site of The Spice of Life since around 1750, although its present incarnation was built in 1898.

But right now it’s an excellent way to spend a Tuesday evening at 19.00 in the heart of Soho enjoying a classic pub quiz. All the action takes place in the downstairs bar at the rear of the pub so please find us there.

An idyllic English pub shared with friends & neighbours. The pub for all seasons, airy and comfortable gastropub just off New Kings Road, not far from Fulham Broadway.

Join them on a cosy Sunday evening at 7pm for a pub quiz.

The Garden Shed boasts two functional event spaces suitable for many occasions. You can choose The Conservatory or The Deck (or both!). A beautiful fairy lit outdoor garden with cushions and heaters welcomes you during the colder months.

Come down at 7.30pm on a Sunday for a bustling pub quiz!

A warm welcome from our hospitable team at The Waterman’s Arms. We are a relaxed neighborhood bar with a stand out food & drink offering a brand new extended bar area, mezzanine, snug & country yard garden will provide the perfect setting for any occasion.

Come on down on a Tuesday evening at 8pm for a quiz and a catch up!

As a McMullen’s house since 1898, and made great in 2018, the Hollybush is a key part of Loughton High Street’s rich history.The Hollybush boasts a contemporary feeling modern high street bar, serving fresh cocktails, plentiful world kegged beer options and a fantastic menu.

At 7pm on a Sunday, pull up a seat and grab a pen for the weekly pub quiz!

The Duke of Sussex Pub & Dining room is a short distance from Chiswick Park station and is situated on the edge of Acton Green Common. Serving a modern menu with a Spanish influence.

Perfect quizzing on a Sunday in Chiswick at 7:30pm!

The Pilgrim hosts many events, birthday celebrations, corporate drinks, sporting events or special occasions.. with large indoor and outdoor space, excellent customer service, happy hour every day and a great location.. what’s not to love about Kennington’s favourite local!

Let’s not forget the popular Sunday quiz, on every Sunday at 7pm.

Situated in the throng of Hammersmith, The Hop Poles is a great choice for any occasion.

Be it grabbing dinner and drinks before laughing for hours at top billed comics at The Apollo or taking in a new show at The Lyric.

Hop Poles also boasts a marvellous pub quiz on a Thursday evening at 7:30pm.

A great place to enjoy a cosy quiz in the heart of National Trust countryside. The Plough Effingham is surrounded by the surrey hills, famous for its most stunning and accessible landscape.

The Plough welcomes you to a monthly quiz on the first Wednesday of every month at 7pm.

venue_name: PUB QUIZ – Hare and Billet, Blackheath – Every Wednesday
notes:
Serving the largest selection of ales in Blackheath, with a beer library including big names to local craft breweries, Hare and Billet have them all.

Come for a cosy, friendly Wednesday night quiz in Blackheath at 8pm.

Dating back to the 1830s, The Bull is rumoured to be built on the site of a house once owned by Sir Walter Raleigh and is one of the most established watering holes in the Islington Upper Street area.

As well as being close to a number of theatre venues, the Bull hosts a marvellous pub quiz on Tuesdays at 8pm!

The Duchy Arms is a pub just a stones throw from Kennington Cross tucked away on Sancroft Street. With a range of casque mark ales which change weekly and a wine list to suit all. You’ll wish you found here sooner!

Wednesdays at 8pm are a particularly good time to come on down, and enjoy a pub quiz!

This lively town centre pub on the banks of the River Lea has been a McMullen house since 1938. Step right off Ware High Street, escape the crowds, relax and unwind on the waterside terrace where you can dine alfresco when the sun permits. Hosting a marvellous pub quiz on Wednesday at 7pm.

A beautiful cozy corner pub/restaurant hidden away behind Chiswick Park station. Originally built in 1885 and named the Railway Tavern for the workers constructing the railway lines nearby, it was renamed The Bollo House back in 2000, after the lane it is on and the underground river it conceals.

Join the Bollo on a Tuesday night at 8pm for a stellar pub quiz!

Located just to the North of Hammersmith Broadway on Shepherd’s Bush Road, this beautiful pub was once surrounded on three sides by the iconic Hammersmith Palais. A colourful pubs with three quirky outdoor drinking areas.

On Tuesdays, the Duke hosts a popular pub quiz at 7.30pm

The Island Queen is a delightful example of an old London gin palace, tucked away on Islington’s quiet backstreets. A colonial-inspired oasis of intrigue, The Island Queen is the perfect setting for a laid-back yet distinctly memorable drinking and dining experience.

Come on in on a Tuesday night for a pub quiz at 8pm!

The Camden Road Arms is a large but still cosy classic Victorian pub, opposite Camden Road station. This pub can do anything from a high-energy Saturday night out to a chilled afternoon roast with your pals, the ultimate pit stop before or after a trip to the famous Camden market.

Come on in on a Tuesday at 7pm for a beer-fuelled pub quiz!

The Star Of The East returns and despite her 160 years, she has never looked so good,

With a bar area, cosy snug, courtyard & beautiful upstairs dining overlooking Canary Wharf. Star of the East aims straight to the heart of the locals, the food lovers, local artists and the proper pint-lovers. We bet you’ll love the ideas we have: the future of this glorious pub is exciting!!!

At 7.30pm on a Tuesday find yourself a spot and settle down for a pub quiz!

This building of Special & Historical Interest set in the historic and delightful Tilehouse Street has been a McMullen house since 1887. Just a moment’s stroll from the bustling town centre, the Cooper’s Arms really is a quality local pub, offering fresh food, hand crafted local ales and barrelfuls of old world charm that make it genuinely relaxing retreat.

Join the Coopers Arms at 7:45pm on a Tuesday eve for a fabulous pub quiz!

The Crabtree is a friendly feeling pub that makes everyone feel welcome, with a spacious updated Victorian interior and an enormous beer garden.

With sweeping Thames views and a fun, lively and well-attended pub quiz night every Tuesday at 8pm, with our bubbly and charming host, Kat, this is a must visit for any West London quizzers!

We highly recommend booking a table for this venue!

A welcoming atmosphere for the whole community. Now well established as something of a gastropub, the Woodman has a fresh and open feel with the light wood, big windows, flowers and art and the beer garden.

Come down on Tuesday evenings at 8pm for their pub quiz!

Built in the early sixteenth century as Place Manor House, the building was later used by King Charles I for his ill fated treaty with Cromwell and Parliament in 1645. The manor house went on to become a coaching inn in the eighteenth century. There is even an album named after the pub by mercury prize nominated band Sweet Billy Pilgrim!

On a Tuesday at 7pm , pop on down for a pub quiz!

Until the early 1900’s Market Square was dominated by grand old ale houses, some dating back to 1643. Dog’s Head is bringing some of this history into the 21st century and giving a second life to one of Stortford’s oldest drinking holes.

At 7.30pm on a Monday, this pub hosts a prize-filled pub quiz!
